horoscopes.intro: November 23 in the stars: Find out what’s in store for you today in our daily horoscopes for Monday November 23. Read the daily horoscopes for your Sun sign or rising sign (ascendant) to plan your day.

aries.text: Your impatient sign prefers green lights above all others, and lucky you, Aries, today you could hit a string of them. A fistbump between the Sagittarius Sun in your fruitful ninth house and miracle-making Neptune in your sign could make your ambitious efforts finally pay off. If a project is still in development, go public with it. Pitch the powers that be, and lead with your deep personal connection to this venture, since that’s what will get people clamoring to come aboard. The world loves a true believer and you’ve never been accused of holding back.

taurus.text: Today the Sagittarius Sun in your soul-searching eighth house trines metaphysical Neptune in your twelfth house of dreams, bringing your loftiest visions into focus. If you’ve been struggling to find direction, carve out time to tune in, whether that’s a meditation app or a long solo walk with your phone on airplane mode. Others may come knocking for your wise counsel, and while you can offer it, don’t give away ALL your hours. Your own breakthrough needs a seat at the table too.

gemini.text: Your chatty sign can get anyone talking, but today the banter could actually lead somewhere. A sultry trine between the Sagittarius Sun in your partnership zone and enchanting Neptune in your eleventh house of friendship has some Geminis turning a suggestive spark into full-blown realization that there’s actually a “there” there. Express your interest and brace yourself for a pleasantly surprising response. But before you make any major declarations, be sure you’re captivated enough to follow up on this lead.

cancer.text: Slow your roll, Cancer! Take a well-deserved break today as the Sun in your sixth house of well-being forms a soothing trine with nurturing Neptune in your career corner. Your devoted sign would put everything aside to “be there” for your people, but the stars are prescribing downtime. Power down early and book something that decreases your stress, like a restorative yoga class or a long soak with a good playlist. If you can shut off your phone by dinnertime, you’ll be amazed at how much you enjoy just being where you are.

leo.text: Take off those rose-colored aviators, Leo! Your big-hearted sign loves to see the best in everyone, and today the Sagittarius Sun in your fifth house of romance aligns with starry-eyed Neptune in your ninth house of big ideas, which could fog up your typically spot-on judgment. If something sounds too good to be true…we don’t have to finish that sentence, do we? Due diligence is your saving grace, so do ALL your research before you sign on the dotted line. A legit opportunity will still be there tomorrow.

virgo.text: Who’s taking care of the caretaker? Your service-oriented sign has been tending to everyone else’s needs, but today the Sagittarius Sun in your foundational fourth house aligns with sensitive Neptune in your emotional eighth, and it’s YOUR turn. Create space to explore your own desires or slip into a creative flow state. If needy loved ones try to bust down your boundaries, let them know you’re off duty for the day (they’ll manage). Schedule something that keeps you centered, whether that’s a sound bath or an evening with a new book and a pot of tea.

libra.text: Just say no to the time-sucking drama queens today! Your people-pleasing sign hates to disappoint anyone, but as the Sagittarius Sun in your communication house aligns with emotional Neptune in your relationship zone, playing savior will only drain your energy and tarnish that shining armor. Instead of rushing to everyone’s rescue, set one firm boundary and spend the freed-up hours on your own interests. Sounds selfish? Hardly. Some of your most profound breakthroughs could come once you stop managing everyone else’s.

scorpio.text: Your psychic channels are open for business today as the Sagittarius Sun in your money house forms a powerful alignment with Neptune in your sixth house of daily routines. Your strategic sign rarely makes a move without a master plan, but if you’ve put your passions on the back burner to pay the bills, it’s time to turn the heat back up. Brainstorm ways to work them into your schedule (or even monetize them). Then set your intentions for the coming months and hit the ground running!

sagittarius.text: Too glam to give a damn? Even your jeans-and-sneakers sign is ready for a dress code today, as the Sun in your sign forms an enchanting alignment with alluring Neptune in your fifth house of glamour and charisma. Your radiance is undeniable, so act and dress the part (new wardrobe additions welcome). Just don’t wear your whole heart on those new silk sleeves, Archer. Conversation will flow freely, but play your cards close to your vest. A little mystery never hurt anyone!

capricorn.text: Some relationships come with an expiration date, and your loyal sign has a habit of ignoring the label. Today the Sagittarius Sun in your twelfth house of endings forms a healing alignment with tender Neptune in your fourth house of roots, and it may be time to close the book on a connection that’s run its course. No need for dramatic bridge burning; a gradual fade may be the kindest way to part. Honor the impact this person had on your life while acknowledging the need to move on. It’s healthier for you both, even if it stings a little.

aquarius.text: Calling all lone wolves! There’s serious strength in numbers today, as the Sagittarius Sun in your eleventh house of teamwork forms a life-affirming trine with profound Neptune in your communication corner. Even your famously independent sign could use some backup, so call in the cavalry. If you’re struggling with a personal issue, round up the friends and relatives who will rally behind you. On the professional front, brainstorm with a few expert collaborators and you could hit on a breakthrough. And if someone asks for your help in return, pay it forward!

pisces.text: Are you satisfied with your lifestyle, Pisces, or just going with the current? Today the Sun in your tenth house of career trines your ruler, Neptune, in your second house of values, launching you on a soul-searching mission. If you’ve drifted from your greatest dreams, sketch out a few actionable steps to get back on track, but don’t rush to implement. Here’s another vital question: Are your people lifting you up? If not, change the conversations you’re having (or start hanging with a new and inspiring crew).

items.title: Effects of Spatial and Spectral Release From Masking on Resource Engagement During Speech-on-Speech Listening
items.originalTitle: Effects of Spatial and Spectral Release From Masking on Resource Engagement During Speech-on-Speech Listening
items.summary: Speech-on-speech listening requires attending to a target talker while ignoring a distractor talker, with performance constrained by both target signal availability and the listener's cognitive resources. , spectral) domain, respectively. However, the effect of spatial vs. spectral RM on listening effort is unknown.
items.caution: A link, not proof of cause.
items.abstract: Speech-on-speech listening requires attending to a target talker while ignoring a distractor talker, with performance constrained by both target signal availability and the listener's cognitive resources. Performance improves with both spatial and spectral release from masking (RM); that is, when the two talkers are separated in either the spatial or the frequency (i.e., spectral) domain, respectively. However, the effect of spatial vs. spectral RM on listening effort is unknown. Participants completed a selective listening task, repeating the speech of one of two simultaneously-presented talkers while having their task-evoked pupil response (TEPR) tracked as a marker of resource engagement. We filtered the target and masker talkers into either non-overlapping (spectral RM) or overlapping (no spectral RM) frequency bands, and presented the two talkers either dichotically (simulating spatial RM) or collocated (no spatial RM). Perceived tiredness, effort, and accuracy ratings were collected during the task. Participants also completed tests to assess three key components of cognition: general intelligence, phonological processing, and working memory. Performance was highest when both forms of RM were available and lowest when neither was available. TEPR was lowest when both forms of RM were available, highest for spectral RM only, and moderate when no RM was available. These results support an inverted U-shaped relationship between effort and performance: listeners allocate resources to maintain performance in moderately difficult conditions and reduce engagement when the task becomes too difficult for further investment to be effective. Higher working memory capacity predicted larger TEPRs and lower perceived tiredness from listening, suggesting that greater cognitive capacity promotes increased resource engagement and might also protect against perceived tiredness.

items.title: Episodic memory consolidation by reactivation of human concept neurons during sleep reflects contents, not sequence of events
items.originalTitle: Episodic memory consolidation by reactivation of human concept neurons during sleep reflects contents, not sequence of events
items.summary: How do our brains manage to store our everyday experiences into memory? Neurons in the human temporal lobe that respond to the concept of an individual person or object have been shown to provide the semantic building blocks for episodic memory.
items.caution: A link, not proof of cause.
items.abstract: How do our brains manage to store our everyday experiences into memory? Neurons in the human temporal lobe that respond to the concept of an individual person or object have been shown to provide the semantic building blocks for episodic memory. Recording from 1415 neurons in neurosurgical patients who learned a story involving specific concepts, we found reactivation of neurons representing these concepts during slow-wave sleep after learning. Concept neurons were conjointly reactivated, particularly during sharp-wave ripples, with time lags suitable for synaptic modification. However, the temporal sequence of reactivation did not reflect the sequence of concepts in the learned story. Unlike rodent place cells, which can acquire preferred firing locations during exploration of new environments according to their pre-existing preferred sequence of activation, human concept neurons are tuned to specific semantic contents before learning starts. Consequently, pre-existing firing sequences correlate with consecutive place fields in rodents, but not with sequences of events in human experience. Thus, in contrast to reactivation of rodent place cells, reactivation of human concept cells does not reflect sequences of events in human experience.

items.title: Implication of the ADCY1 Gene in Lithium Response in Bipolar Disorder by Genome-Wide Association Meta-Analysis
items.originalTitle: Implication of the ADCY1 Gene in Lithium Response in Bipolar Disorder by Genome-Wide Association Meta-Analysis
items.summary: Efforts to examine the influence of genetics in the efficacy of lithium using genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified several loci. Here, we report new cases and meta-analyses to combine previous efforts.
items.caution: Strongest kind of evidence — still check who took part.
items.abstract:
Objectives: Efforts to examine the influence of genetics in the efficacy of lithium using genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified several loci. Here, we report new cases and meta-analyses to combine previous efforts.

Methods: We report data from 1259 participants with bipolar disorder (BD) recruited at University College London who had been treated with lithium. The data come from three waves of genotyping on different arrays. The GWAS data from each array was analysed separately and then meta-analysed with two published lithium response GWAS datasets. Post-GWAS analyses were conducted to examine lithium response heritability and its genetic correlations with other traits. We also attempted to replicate past polygenic risk scores (PRS) results.

Results: SNP rs116927879 (A/G) was associated with lithium response at a genome-wide significance level (p = 4.509 × 10-08) with a consistent effect across all cohorts. rs116927879 is located on chromosome 7 and maps to the protein-coding gene ADCY1 and two pseudo-genes, GTF2IP13 and SEPT7P2. The sQTL results suggested that rs116927879 genotypes may influence the splicing of ADCY1 across different brain regions. We estimated the SNP heritability (h2) for good lithium response as 20.3% and 15.6% for subjective/objective response definitions, respectively. We did not observe any genetic correlation or PRS association between the lithium response and schizophrenia or major depression disorder. However, we found weak evidence to suggest that males are more likely to be good responders.

Conclusions: Our GWAS identifies a genome-wide significant finding and provides updated heritability estimates for lithium efficacy.

items.title: Surgical versus conservative management of acute subdural hematoma in elderly patients: a systematic review of functional outcomes and prognostic factors
items.originalTitle: Surgical versus conservative management of acute subdural hematoma in elderly patients: a systematic review of functional outcomes and prognostic factors
items.summary: Management of acute subdural hematoma in the elderly requires nuanced clinical decision-making. While the Brain Trauma Foundation incorporates clot thickness and midline shift in their ASDH management guidelines, they do not quote an age bracket cut-off.
items.caution: Strongest kind of evidence — still check who took part.
items.abstract: Management of acute subdural hematoma in the elderly requires nuanced clinical decision-making. While the Brain Trauma Foundation incorporates clot thickness and midline shift in their ASDH management guidelines, they do not quote an age bracket cut-off. Evidence to date suggests the elderly see disproportionately high morbidity and mortality regardless of surgical or conservative management. To systematically review the evidence comparing surgical evacuation versus conservative management of ASDH in elderly patients and assess the impact of patient factors on outcomes, a systematic review was conducted examining six observational studies (n = 812) comparing surgical and conservative management of traumatic ASDH in patients aged 60 or older. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, 6-month mortality, and functional outcomes. MEDLINE, Embase and CINAHL were searched up to December 2025. Risk of bias assessment was performed using the Newcastle Ottawa Scale. Results were presented descriptively and synthesized narratively by outcome timepoint as clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Surgery was not consistently associated with improved mortality nor improved functional outcomes. Surgical patients presented with worse clinical and radiological severity. In-hospital mortality analysis of three cohorts demonstrated substantial heterogeneity, with relative risks ranging from 1.37 to 13.63, favoring conservative management. Six-month mortality showed even greater heterogeneity with directionally inconsistent findings. Functional outcomes, when reported, either favored conservative management or were neutral. Current evidence does not establish a consistent mortality or functional advantage for surgical evacuation of ASDH in elderly patients. Patients with poor neurological status demonstrate high mortality regardless of intervention, while those with mild neurological impairment may not derive meaningful benefit from surgery. Future prospective studies should standardize frailty assessment alongside clinical and radiographic parameters to identify where true clinical equipoise exists and establish guidelines in this distinct patient population. No funding was received for this review.

items.title: Return to Sport Following Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction in Martial Arts and Combat Sports: A Systematic Review
items.originalTitle: Return to Sport Following Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction in Martial Arts and Combat Sports: A Systematic Review
items.summary: Physical demands in martial arts and combat sports put substantial stress on the knee, particularly the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL). ACL injuries are highly debilitating in these sports, yet return-to-sport (RTS) data remains sparse.
items.caution: Strongest kind of evidence — still check who took part.
items.source: HSS journal : the musculoskeletal journal of Hospital for Special Surgery
items.abstract:
Background: Physical demands in martial arts and combat sports put substantial stress on the knee, particularly the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL). ACL injuries are highly debilitating in these sports, yet return-to-sport (RTS) data remains sparse.

Purpose: We sought to investigate: (1) What are the RTS rates and timelines for combat athletes following ACL reconstruction (ACLR)? (2) How does ACLR impact post-operative performance metrics? (3) What is the risk profile for subsequent ACL injury?

Methods: We conducted a systematic review of PubMed, Scopus, Embase, SPORTDiscus, and Google Scholar through February 22, 2026, for clinical studies reporting RTS, performance, or secondary injury metrics following ACLR in martial arts and combat sport athletes.

Results: Six studies met the inclusion criteria (338 total ACLRs). Initial RTS rates to any participation were high (76.9%-86.3%), but durable return was less consistent when using stricter endpoints, such as Ultimate Fighting Championship sustained return (≥2 fights: 56.3%) or return to preinjury competitive levels (57.7%). One professional fighter study reported a significant postoperative decline, including a reduction in strike evasion among these athletes. Among studies reporting secondary ACL injury or subsequent ACL surgery, rates ranged from 13.1% to 20.0%. Fear of reinjury was a notable psychological barrier to return.

Conclusion: The findings of this systematic review of Level-III and Level-IV studies suggest that return to training for combat athletes after ACLR is achievable, but durable return to elite or preinjury competition is less consistently demonstrated and carries substantial secondary injury risk.

Level of evidence: Level IV: systematic review of Level-III and Level-IV studies.

items.title: Implementation intention intervention for enhancing executive control in baseball players' competitive scenes
items.originalTitle: Implementation intention intervention for enhancing executive control in baseball players' competitive scenes
items.summary: This study investigates the intervention effect of implementation intentions on executive control in baseball players within competitive scenarios, utilizing a combination of behavioral assessments and functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (fNIRS).
items.caution: Strongest kind of evidence — still check who took part.
items.abstract:
Background: This study investigates the intervention effect of implementation intentions on executive control in baseball players within competitive scenarios, utilizing a combination of behavioral assessments and functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (fNIRS).

Methods: Thirty baseball players were randomly assigned to an experimental group (receiving implementation intention training) or a control group (undergoing a neutral task).

Results: Behavioral data revealed that the experimental group exhibited significantly shorter reaction times in go/nogo tasks post-intervention, while fNIRS measurements demonstrated enhanced activation in left ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (vIPFC) of the experimental group compared to the control group.

Conclusions: Under the conditions of this small-sample exploratory study, athletes showed a declining trend in abnormal inhibitory-control-related brain activation under competitive contexts following implementation intentions intervention, which preliminarily hints at a potential improvement in their executive control performance in competitive situations.

items.title: Electrical Vestibular Stimulation in Primary and Comorbid Insomnia: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
items.originalTitle: Electrical Vestibular Stimulation in Primary and Comorbid Insomnia: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
items.summary: Insomnia is a common disorder associated with impaired daytime functioning and psychiatric comorbidities such as anxiety and depression. Electrical vestibular nerve stimulation (VeNS) has emerged as a potential nonpharmacological treatment due to the vestibular system's role in sleep regulation.
items.caution: Strongest kind of evidence — still check who took part.
items.abstract:
Background: Insomnia is a common disorder associated with impaired daytime functioning and psychiatric comorbidities such as anxiety and depression. Electrical vestibular nerve stimulation (VeNS) has emerged as a potential nonpharmacological treatment due to the vestibular system's role in sleep regulation.

Objective: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of VeNS versus sham stimulation in reducing insomnia severity, improving sleep quality and quality of life, and alleviating anxiety symptoms in adults with primary or psychiatric comorbid insomnia.

Materials and methods: In total, 6 databases were systematically searched from inception to September 2025, following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Randomized sham-controlled trials evaluating VeNS for insomnia were included. Random-effects models estimated mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), and heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 .

Results: Of the 5 studies included, three were on primary insomnia (n = 310) and 2, on psychiatric comorbid insomnia (n = 120). The use of VeNS significantly reduced insomnia severity index scores in both primary (mean difference [MD]: -3.42; 95%CI: -6.58 to -0.26) and psychiatric comorbid (MD: -5.51; 95%CI: -8.49 to -2.52) cases. Greater benefits were observed in younger adults. While this treatment did not significantly improve global sleep quality, it did improve quality-of-life domains including vitality, mental health, and physical functioning. Anxiety symptoms were also significantly reduced. Adverse events were mild and infrequent, with no consistent device-related serious events reported.

Conclusion: The use of VeNS may reduce insomnia severity and anxiety with good tolerability. However, evidence is limited by small sample sizes and substantial heterogeneity. Larger, high-quality, randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these findings.

items.title: Evaluating the Role of Visceral Adiposity in Neurological Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.originalTitle: Evaluating the Role of Visceral Adiposity in Neurological Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.summary: Neurological disorders represent a major global health challenge. According to recent Global Burden of Disease (GBD) estimates, Alzheimer's disease and other dementias, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, and headache disorders together account for nearly 3% of the worldwide disease burden.
items.caution: Strongest kind of evidence — still check who took part.
items.abstract:
Background: Neurological disorders represent a major global health challenge. According to recent Global Burden of Disease (GBD) estimates, Alzheimer's disease and other dementias, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, and headache disorders together account for nearly 3% of the worldwide disease burden. While visceral adipose tissue has traditionally been viewed as a metabolic concern, emerging evidence highlights visceral adiposity as an independent risk factor and potential contributor to the pathogenesis and progression of several neurological disorders.

Materials and methods: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines to evaluate the association between visceral adiposity and neurological disorders. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251083846). A comprehensive search of PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science was performed in June 2025. Eligibility criteria were defined using the PICOS framework. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), adapted for cross-sectional designs where applicable. Adjusted effect estimates were pooled using a random-effects model.

Results: A total of 26 studies involving 1, 059, 075 participants were included; approximately 96% of participants were female, largely because of one nationwide female-only cohort, and mean ages ranged from 44.5 to 78.3 years. Twenty-three studies (88.5%) reported at least one adverse association between greater visceral or central adiposity and poorer neurological or cognitive outcomes.The meta-analysis of 12 studies showed that elevated visceral adiposity was associated with a 48% higher likelihood of adverse neurological outcomes (pooled effect estimate [OR/HR] = 1.48, 95% CI: 1.27-1.72, p < 0.001; I2 = 83%). Significant associations were observed for stroke-related outcomes (OR = 1.41, 95% CI: 1.15-1.74), young-onset dementia (HR = 1.55, 95% CI: 1.34-1.79), and migraine (OR = 1.41, 95% CI: 1.05-1.88), whereas the pooled estimate for subclinical cerebrovascular imaging findings was elevated but imprecise (OR = 3.49, 95% CI: 0.64-19.10).

Conclusion: Elevated visceral adiposity is associated with a higher risk of stroke-related outcomes, dementia, migraine, and adverse brain imaging findings. items.originalTitle: Pharmacological and non-pharmacological management of sleep disturbances in Alzheimer's disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis
items.summary: BackgroundSleep disturbances affect half of Alzheimer's disease patients, accelerating cognitive decline and increasing caregiver burden.

items.abstract: BackgroundSleep disturbances affect half of Alzheimer's disease patients, accelerating cognitive decline and increasing caregiver burden. The comparative effectiveness of available interventions remains unclear.ObjectiveTo compare pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions on sleep outcomes in Alzheimer's disease using network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs).MethodsFollowing PRISMA and a registered PROSPERO protocol (CRD420250653178), four databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, Web of Science) were searched through July 2026 for RCTs. Pairwise and frequentist random-effects network meta-analyses using Hedges' g were performed for six sleep outcomes: total sleep time (TST), wake after sleep onset (WASO), nocturnal awakenings (NoA), sleep efficiency, daytime sleep, and daytime naps. A Bayesian network meta-analysis served as a sensitivity analysis.ResultsTwelve RCTs (N = 936, 32 study arms) were included. Zolpidem and zopiclone reduced sleep fragmentation, with improvements in NoA (SMD -1.09) and WASO (SMD -0.86), although these findings were based on a single short-term trial. Suvorexant increased TST (SMD 0.376) and increased TST (SMD 0.376), while lemborexant 2.5 mg reduced NoA (SMD -0.98), with favorable short-term tolerability. Walking (SMD -0.48), bright light therapy (SMD -0.37), and NITE-AD (SMD -0.52) reduced NoA, while combined light therapy and melatonin reduced daytime sleep (SMD -0.858). Melatonin monotherapy, trazodone, and mirtazapine showed limited or inconsistent effects.ConclusionsNon-pharmacological interventions may be considered before pharmacological treatment. When pharmacotherapy is required, dual orexin receptor antagonists may be useful for selected sleep outcomes, whereas Z-drugs should be used cautiously given their established safety concerns. Larger, longer-duration head-to-head trials using standardized sleep outcomes are needed.

items.title: Effects of a Combined Mindfulness-Based, Virtual Reality-Assisted and Cognitive-Behavioral Sexual Counselling Program on Sexual Function, Sexual Quality of Life and Sexual Health Literacy in Infertile Women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Randomized Controlled Trial
items.originalTitle: Effects of a Combined Mindfulness-Based, Virtual Reality-Assisted and Cognitive-Behavioral Sexual Counselling Program on Sexual Function, Sexual Quality of Life and Sexual Health Literacy in Infertile Women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Randomized Controlled Trial
items.summary: Infertile women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) face overlapping hormonal, psychological and relational burdens that threaten sexual function; evidence on integrated psychosexual care is scarce.
items.caution: Strongest kind of evidence — still check who took part.
items.abstract:
Background: Infertile women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) face overlapping hormonal, psychological and relational burdens that threaten sexual function; evidence on integrated psychosexual care is scarce.

Objective: To evaluate whether an eight-session program combining mindfulness, relaxation-oriented virtual reality (VR) and cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) improves sexual function, sexual quality of life and sexual health literacy vs usual care.

Methods: In this single-center randomized trial in Kashan, Iran, 80 married infertile women with PCOS were randomized (block size 4) to the program (n = 40; eight individual sessions, twice weekly) or usual care (n = 40). The Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI; primary outcome), Sexual Quality of Life-Female (SQOL-F) and Sexual Health Literacy for Adults (SHELA) questionnaires were completed at baseline, 4 and 8 weeks. Groups were compared with baseline-adjusted ANCOVA. All participants were analyzed.

Results: Retention was 100%. Adjusted FSFI differences favored the program at 4 weeks (3.20, 95% CI 1.18 to 5.23) and 8 weeks (7.78, 95% CI 5.69 to 9.86; Hedges g 1.40). At 8 weeks, SQOL-F (12.16, 95% CI 7.90 to 16.41) and SHELA (13.17, 95% CI 9.41 to 16.94) were also higher; the 4-week SQOL-F difference was imprecise (4.31, 95% CI -0.38 to 9.00). At 8 weeks, 20.0% vs 77.5% scored at or below the FSFI cut-off (26.55). FSFI fell by 3.54 points in usual care, accounting for 46% of the 8-week difference in mean change. Four-week effects were less robust than 8-week effects.

Conclusions: In this unblinded trial, the program was associated with large improvements in all three outcomes at 8 weeks vs usual care, partly reflecting deterioration in controls. Because the comparator offered no equivalent contact, the findings reflect the whole program, not specific effects of mindfulness, CBT or VR. Attention-controlled multicenter trials with longer follow-up are needed.
